name: PyATS Write Baseline
notes:
# PyATS Write Baseline

## Purpose
Records a pre-change baseline of the network. It loads the devices of the Nautobot inventory `LAB`, runs a pyATS snapshot (all features) on each device with fan-out (up to 10 devices at a time), joins the results with Fan In, pulls the git repository, stores one JSON snapshot file per device, and then commits and pushes once. Use it before a change to capture the state you may need to compare against later.

## Assumptions / prerequisites
* credentials: 'cisco - noc' (SSH, used by the pyATS testbed), 'pyats' and 'nautobot' (token), 'gitea' (token for the git repository)
* inventory: 'LAB' (filter inventory, global scope)
* git repository: 'gitea' (category device_configs)
* nautobot: source 'nautobot'
* pyats: source 'pyats'

## Gotchas
* Writes to git and pushes to the remote 'gitea' repository. The push cannot be undone from the canvas.
* Fan-out starts at Get from Nautobot (one child per device, max 10 concurrent). Fan In (Fan In, fan-in) joins them before Git Pull.
* Store Artifact (store-artifact) runs after Fan In so that the run creates one commit. Its own commit and push flags are off; Git Push (git-push) makes the single commit and push.
* Store Artifact `content_source` is `pyats_snapshot`. This value is not in the step's documented list (running_config, startup_config, command_output, latest_command_output, rendered_template, merged_content, comparison_diff). Check it before running, because the file content depends on it.
* Store Artifact `parsed_output_key` holds a secret placeholder instead of an output key. The field only applies when `content_source` is `rendered_template`, so it should be cleared or checked.
* Store Artifact writes to `snapshots/` in the repository, one file per device, named `{device.name}_snapshot_baseline.json`.

## Example
For a device named `LAB-SW1`, this run writes `snapshots/LAB-SW1_snapshot_baseline.json` into git repository 'gitea' and creates one commit with one push for the whole run. With N devices in inventory `LAB`, it writes N files in that single commit.

data.title: Get from Nautobot
data.overview: Select devices from the Nautobot inventory.
data.description: Select one or more target devices from the inventory.

data.title: Add Testbed
data.overview: Build a pyATS testbed from the current device list.
data.description: Resolve a credential and pyATS shim source for the current device list, producing a reusable testbed bundle that downstream pyATS-backed steps (e.g. Get & Parse Config) consume without needing their own credential/source configuration.

data.title: Get Snapshot
data.overview: Capture a Genie "learn" snapshot of live device state.
data.description: Learn one or more Genie features (BGP, OSPF, interfaces, platform, ...) or "all" via pyATS and store the structured snapshot. Requires an upstream Add Testbed step.

data.title: Fan In
data.overview: Rejoin fan-out branches into one execution path.
data.description: Rejoin a fanned-out workflow into a single path. Per-device steps run in parallel child workflows up to this node; steps placed after it run once over all devices. Place git / store-artifact steps after Fan In for safe, single-commit exports.

data.title: Git Pull
data.overview: Pull latest changes for a git source.
data.description: Pull the latest changes for a configured git source. Fan-out note: a per-repo advisory lock (services/git/repo_lock.py) serialises concurrent callers -- fan-out children or independent sibling branches in one run -- against the same source, so the working tree is not corrupted.

data.title: Store Artifact
data.description: Persist generated content such as backups, reports, or logs. Fan-out note: the filesystem sink writes a shared destination; concurrent child workflows can still race on the same path -- prefer per-device path templates or disable fan-out when using it. The git sink holds a per-repo advisory lock (services/git/repo_lock.py) across concurrent callers -- fan-out children or independent sibling branches in one run -- so the working tree is not corrupted, but each caller still opens its own commit; place it after a Fan In node (or other join point) for one commit, not N.

data.title: Git Push
data.overview: Commit and push changes to git remote.
data.description: Commit exported changes and push them to the configured git source remote. Fan-out note: a per-repo advisory lock (services/git/repo_lock.py) serialises concurrent callers -- fan-out children or independent sibling branches in one run -- against the same source, so the working tree is not corrupted. Each caller still produces its own commit/push though; prefer a single push after a Fan In node, or unique branches/paths per caller, if you want exactly one.
